protocol.description:
This protocol extends ext-image-copy-capture-v1 so that a client which only shows a small preview of a capture source, such as a thumbnail of a window or an output, can ask the compositor for a smaller image. The compositor then scales the source down while drawing it, straight into the client's buffer, instead of handing over a full-size image for the client to shrink.
The protocol only changes the buffer constraints of a session and the size of the images it fills: frames, damage, transforms, cursor painting and alpha follow ext-image-copy-capture-v1 exactly as for a full-size session.

interface.name: zoolander_image_copy_capture_size_manager_v1
interface.description: Gives image copy capture sessions a maximum image size.

request.name: destroy
request.description: Destroys the manager. Objects created through it remain valid.

request.name: get_session_size

description.summary: control the image size of a capture session

request.description:
Creates an object that sets the maximum image size of a capture session.
The session may have been created from any capture source: an output, a toplevel, a workspace or anything else the compositor captures. More than one object may be created for the same session; the most recent set_max_size request through any of them is the one in effect.

interface.name: zoolander_image_copy_capture_session_size_v1

description.summary: maximum image size of a capture session

interface.description:
Sets the largest image a capture session may produce.
Until set_max_size is sent the session keeps the full source size.

request.name: destroy
request.description: Destroys the object. The session keeps the maximum size last set.

request.name: set_max_size
request.description:
Sets the maximum width and height, in buffer pixels, of the images of the session. Zero means no limit in that dimension, so (0, 0) restores the full source size.
From then on the buffer_size the session advertises is the source size fitted inside the maximum size with the source's aspect ratio kept: when the source is no larger than the maximum in either dimension it is the source size, since the image is never scaled up; otherwise it is the largest size of the source's aspect ratio that fits, with the scaled dimension rounded to the nearest pixel and at least 1. When the source's size changes, as when a toplevel is resized, the fitted size follows it.
If this changes the buffer constraints, the compositor sends them again at once, ending with ext_image_copy_capture_session_v1.done, and a frame captured with a buffer of the old size fails with buffer_constraints. A client that sends this request right after creating the session sees the full-size constraints first and should allocate buffers after the last done event.
The compositor draws the whole source scaled down into the buffer, for shared-memory and dma-buf buffers alike. Damage is reported in the buffer's own coordinates.
The request has no effect once the session is stopped or destroyed.
